independent.summary: 'self-hosted draws down an allowance' uses a hard-coded `cost < 2_000` bound against the SELF_HOSTED_PRICE that was computed when the module was imported, so it reads whatever STEADFAST_WATTS/STEADFAST_KWH_RATE are set in the environment. At baseline the fixture costs about 776 micros, so any retariff above roughly 2.6x the baseline (e.g. STEADFAST_KWH_RATE=0.45) fails the suite. That contradicts the file header's promise that selection tests 'compare against the exported constant... so retariffing the box does not break them'.

'the self-hosted rate is above zero but well below the cheapest cloud model' only compares `SELF_HOSTED_PRICE.in` against the cheapest listed input rate. It never checks `.out`, so a derivation that pushed the self-hosted output rate above every cloud output rate would still pass, even though the test name and message claim self-hosted is cheaper than any cloud model.

grades.reason: 'delivers only to clients in the matching workspace' already connects two clients in one workspace and an outsider in another, then asserts the outsider gets zero write attempts; the exclusion and no-target groups cover cross-workspace delivery as well. Line 362 is just the end of the file.

The 'doubling the tariff' and 'halving the draw' tests re-import the module with changed env vars and pin exact derived values (0.07/1.572 and 0.0175/0.393), so wrong derivation logic in pricing.js would fail them.

summary: Both local findings are generic 'test doesn't verify X' claims that the diff plainly contradicts, and the model missed the two real (minor) weaknesses in the pricing tests.
